text:
Maya: starting a canary for quant-slim-v2 on /v1/generate this afternoon. want to make the automatic fallback gates explicit before we flip traffic. TL;DR: fallback if quality drops >2% on the small eval set OR p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for longer than 5m. ok?

Liam: ok as a first pass. couple of quick tradeoffs: 1) 2% quality delta is tight for short windows (sample noise), 2) should we prefer request-level fallback (retry to baseline) vs route-level rollback?

Maya: good call. thinking hybrid: try per-request replay to baseline for user-facing low-latency endpoints, and full route rollback for sustained regressions. keeps UX smooth and avoids mass thrash.

Raj: agree. also need to account for session affinity — if we replay to baseline we must preserve session state / KV cache handles or we risk context mismatch. Can we do a transparent proxy that attaches the same session id to baseline?

Dana: technical note: baseline model doesn't accept the same quantized KV format right now. replay will have to rehydrate context from raw tokens. small perf hit but ok for occasional retries. We should limit retries to 1 per request.

Maya: yeah limit 1 retry. also add a circuit budget so we don't overload baseline during large regressions. budget = concurrent_replays: 50, burst: 100. if exceeded, fall back to route rollback.

Liam: what metrics/doors do we wire into the rollout controller? propose: generated_quality_delta (avg over 5m), p95_latency_ratio, error_rate, replay_success_rate. threshold config in rollout YAML.

Maya: ^ please add signal for "semantic-regression-alert" from eval-runner (we run small synthetic prompts and classifier checks). if that fires, immediate rollback.

Raj: sample rollout config (proto):
```yaml
rollout: quant-slim-v2
traffic:
  start_pct: 1
  target_pct: 10
  step_minutes: 15
gates:
  - name: latency_p95_ratio
    window: 5m
    threshold: 1.5
  - name: quality_delta_pct
    window: 5m
    threshold: 2
  - name: semantic_regression_alert
    immediate: true
retries:
  per_request: 1
  concurrent_replay_budget: 50
  overflow_action: rollback_route
```

Dana: love it. add a config flag allow_session_replay: true|false so teams with incompatible baselines can disable per-request replay and just do route rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary quant-slim-v2 -> 1% on /v1/generate by maya at 4532109901 :rocket:

Maya: deployed. I'll watch the small eval runner and logs. tagging @SRE-Oncall for visibility.

SRE-Oncall: pinged. I'll also add an alert for concurrent_replay_budget > 80% so we can intervene before baseline overload. what's the plan for cache invalidation? if we failover and then restore, do we flush certain caches?

Raj: good question — plan is soft-ttl for the per-canary session cache (30m). on rollback we keep cache but mark entries as "canary-stale" for 10m to avoid hot-swapping incompatible representations. full flush only on major model change.

Liam: one more ops detail: telemetry tags. include rollout_id and variant in all traces and token-cost logs so we can slice unit economics quickly. also surface per-variant latency by sequence length bucket.

Maya: agreed. final checklist before we expand to 10%:
- [ ] add semantic_regression alert to controller
- [ ] set replay_budget alert (SRE)
- [ ] telemetry tagging (engine)
- [ ] allow_session_replay flag default true

Dana: i'll make the PR to add allow_session_replay and the tag instrumentation. aiming to merge in 2 hours.

Maya: perfect. if anything flares, fallback behavior is: 1) per-request to baseline up to budget, 2) if sustained -> controller auto-rolls back route and posts a message here with rollback reason.

Raj: maybe add a short human confirmation window for rollbacks triggered by semantic_regression_alert (30s) to allow noisy alerts to be investigated? immediate = true is scary.

Maya: i'm fine with 30s guard, but not longer. we risk letting bad outputs go out. 30s ok.

SRE-Oncall: noted. i'll reduce budget alert thresholds and add the 30s silencing window for semantic alerts in the controller config.

Maya: thanks team. will post a quick follow-up with links to the rollout dashboard and the eval run results in 5m. :thumbsup:
